resources.string: Looks like you\'re indoors. We suggest logging on the trail: it keeps where you live out of the data, and it measures the signal where people will need it.
Public heatmaps have revealed where people live. Start %1$s away from home.

Pressing %1$s records samples and shares them: what is recorded is sent to our server. No sample is recorded until you press %1$s, and recording stops when you press %2$s, when the phone shuts down, or at 10%% battery.

Each sample holds the position and time, the time since the phone was turned on, the location\'s horizontal and vertical accuracy, its altitude and whether it was simulated, and for each SIM its slot, carrier, service state, network type, signal readings and the IDs of the cell towers it hears, with when each was measured. It also carries a random app ID made on this phone, a random ID for each recording and another for each sample, and the version of the sample format. A sample never holds your name, phone number, accounts, IMEI or Android ID.

Samples are sent automatically when recording stops and when you open the app. Without a connection, the app keeps trying until they are sent, and until then they stay on this phone. Lines the app can\'t read, such as samples from an old version of the app, are never sent and stay on this phone. The app also keeps a copy of the most recent sample recorded on this phone, even after it is sent, so “See the data sent” can show it; the copy itself is never sent. On our server they are private and never published. Each sample is deleted 90 days after it arrives.

To send samples, the app connects to Firebase, the Google service that receives them, and signs in there with an anonymous account made for the app on this phone; Firebase keeps that account\'s random ID and sign-in times. Every connection shows Google the phone\'s IP address, and the Firebase libraries also send the phone\'s language and country setting and codes for its brand, model and Android version. The app also asks Google Play to confirm that it is the real app, on a real phone.
The samples themselves are not anonymous: the random app ID links one phone\'s samples, so under Brazil\'s data protection law (LGPD) they are personal data.

The public map, at alexandreffaria.github.io/tem-sinal, is anonymous. It shows only totals per small area (hexagons about 50 m across) and carrier: signal strength, network type, how often there was service, emergency calls only or no service, and the month last seen. No app ID, recording, exact time or exact point is published. At least 300 m is left out around any place where the phone stayed still for 30 minutes or more near the start or end of a recording, such as home. A shorter stop, like parking at a trailhead, is kept, so start and stop recording away from home.

This is exactly what leaves the phone for the most recent sample recorded here: the text the app sends to our server, with the app ID and recording ID. The app keeps a copy of this one sample on the phone to show it here. Samples on the server stay private; only totals per area are ever public.
No sample has been recorded on this phone yet. Press %1$s, and the next sample will show here.
Checking the server for older recordings…
Couldn\'t check the server for older recordings. Try again when you\'re online.
It is deleted from our server now and from the map at the next daily update. This can\'t be undone.
Being recorded now. Press STOP to delete it.
Couldn\'t delete. Try again when you\'re online.

Nothing was deleted: our server holds nothing of this recording with this app\'s ID, so it was taken off the list. Either its samples have expired, after 90 days, without any of them reaching the map, or it was sent before the app was reinstalled or its data was cleared, with an ID this app no longer has.
Logging needs precise location. Allow precise location for this app in Settings.
Logging needs location access. Allow location for this app in Settings.
Logging needs phone access to read your SIM. Allow Phone for this app in Settings.
Logging stopped to save battery for calls. Everything logged so far is kept on this phone and will be sent.
